props.title: Bulletproof
props.initialSlug: Mismatched cop & crook become unlikely allies

sections.content: Bulletproof represents peak 90s buddy-cop action comedy, pairing Damon Wayans and Adam Sandler in their prime. It follows the formula established by 48 Hrs. (1982) and Lethal Weapon (1987), but adds its own irreverent humor. Director Ernest Dickerson, who previously worked as Spike Lee's cinematographer on classics like Do the Right Thing (1989), brings solid action chops while letting the leads' chemistry drive the story. The film sits at an interesting intersection between Sandler's goofball comedies like Billy Madison (1995) and grittier 90s action fare.

sections.content: The mid-90s marked a specific moment when action comedies could still be R-rated and genuinely violent while incorporating broad humor. Films like Bad Boys (1995) and The Last Boy Scout (1991) walked this line, mixing legitimate action sequences with character-driven comedy. Bulletproof follows this template, though it leans harder into comedy than most. It's part of a subset of buddy films where one partner betrays the other - like Tango & Cash (1989) and Point Break (1991) - but plays it for laughs rather than drama.

Director Ernest Dickerson's background in serious films like Juice (1992) gives the action sequences more weight than typical comedy fare. The film's mix of tones - from slapstick to genuine violence - reflects a Hollywood era before the PG-13 rating completely dominated action movies. You can draw a direct line from Bulletproof to later buddy comedies like Rush Hour (1998) and The Other Guys (2010), though those films played it safer with their ratings and content. sections.content: Bulletproof marks a transition point between the harder-edged action comedies of the 80s like Beverly Hills Cop (1984) and the more family-friendly fare that would dominate the late 90s and 2000s. The film's violence and R-rating feel almost quaint now, when most action comedies aim for PG-13 to maximize audience reach. You can see the genre's evolution from Midnight Run (1988) through Bulletproof to modern entries like Central Intelligence (2016).
